source.title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
source.authors: Christian A. Rogers; Qian Lin; Daniel S. Brown

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies SAE analysis to an OpenVLA robot policy and reports results on outcome prediction and feature interpretation. This extends the SAE-feature evidence to a VLA setting; it does not test toy-model superposition geometry or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on SAE-based outcome prediction, feature–outcome associations, and description validation, which bear on V4. It does not measure overlapping feature directions, feature sparsity/importance transitions, neuron capacity allocation, or feature dimensionality. Discussion and cited results about prior work are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The paper uses a TopK SAE (2,048 features, K=64) on OpenVLA layer-0 residual activations, mean-pooled over image tokens, as a tool for outcome prediction and behaviour interpretation. It reports only its own pipeline's performance: SAE vs raw-activation outcome AUROC, top-30 success rates of outcome-selected features, and VLM detection scoring of its generated descriptions. It does not measure whether OpenVLA represents features in superposition. There is no reconstruction or variance-explained metric, no comparison of SAE features against neurons for monosemanticity, and no test of feature spread across neurons. Superposition appears only as cited motivation (Appendix B.2). So the results do not bear on V4 or any other version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the authors treat the description method as validated only in aggregate and individual descriptions as hypotheses (±0.2 CI with 24 clips per pair). They also read features as outcome markers rather than causes.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a TopK SAE and evaluates outcome prediction and feature descriptions in a VLA policy; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method or its geometry/sparsity sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-description specificity varies across feature–task pairs; the paper notes task-dependent interpretation for feature 480 and uneven validation scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Some outcome-selected SAE features in OpenVLA (layer 0, mean-pooled image tokens) admit VLM descriptions that predict held-out activations better than shuffled descriptions on 11 of 12 pairs. The per-pair results are uneven: feature 850 is anti-correlated and feature 132 is non-specific.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in a VLA robot policy correspond to describable behavioural events associated with task outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features preserve the outcome-predictive information of raw OpenVLA activations (AUROC 0.81 vs 0.80), and individual features' top-30 trajectories are strongly skewed toward success or failure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decomposition of VLA activations retains outcome-predictive information and yields outcome-associated features.

record.problems: The study uses one VLA model and 500 rollouts, with 95 held out. Feature success rates are based on each feature's selected top 30 trajectories. Description validation is uneven; with 24 clips per pair, the paper estimates an individual AUROC confidence interval of roughly ±0.2. Recoverability estimates use four branches per probe and are described by the authors as coarse and policy-specific.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. The text's majority-baseline accuracy curves and alarm-threshold table concern outcome prediction/actionability rather than whether SAE features are recoverable or interpretable, so they are not cataloged as V4 feature results.

untested.parts: Toy-model geometry, near-orthogonal overlapping directions and sparsity-dependent transitions: not studied.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity: not studied.
Polysemanticity without capacity pressure: not studied.
No neuron-level spread analysis, no SAE reconstruction or fidelity metric, and no comparison of SAE features with neurons. The SAE is used only as a tool.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features (across seeds, sizes or interventions): not studied. Only a task-dependent meaning of feature 480 is noted.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T3 with V4 'supports' is rejected. Superposition is invoked only as cited motivation for using an SAE. The SAE is unusual: layer-0 residual stream, averaged over image tokens, 2,048 features, trained on 500 rollouts. No reconstruction or fidelity number is reported. The r11 note misattributes the '28 of 30' statement, which belongs to feature 1578.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The paper does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from features competing for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The paper does not test whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE-recovered sparse features in OpenVLA, a VLA model, not a range of standard LLMs. It does not test whether features are spread across many neurons.
The paper evaluates descriptions of selected SAE features, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical model units across models, seeds, or interventions.
The SAE associates each feature with an activation direction, but the paper does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features or test feature geometry.

rows.measure: AUROC for predicting eventual outcome
rows.note: The paper says the SAE and raw-activation AUROCs are nearly identical. SAE has 2,048 features with K = 64.

rows.subject: OpenVLA-7B
rows.operation_detail: Scores automatically generated SAE-feature descriptions on held-out clips using a VLM judge that sees the description.
rows.measure: Description-based detection AUROC
rows.uncertainty: Mean AUROC 95% CI [0.64, 0.87]; ΔAUROC 95% CI over clips [0.10, 0.24], widening to [−0.01, 0.35] when resampling pairs as well; permutation p < 0.001; sign test p = 0.003
rows.note: Descriptions outperform shuffled descriptions on 11 of 12 pairs; the authors say specificity varies across features.
rows.check: Aggregate validation of the study's VLM description pipeline (mean AUROC 0.76 vs 0.58 shuffled). The pair-resampled ΔAUROC CI [-0.01, 0.35] crosses zero. This measures pipeline performance, not superposition.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-feature outcome prediction and outcome-associated feature activation in OpenVLA
reader_labels.reason: SAE features predict trajectory outcome with AUROC 0.81, attain AUROC 0.71 before the estimated PNR, and several individual features show strong outcome associations (r1–r12).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Aggregate held-out description validation and feature–task pairs with positive description advantage
reader_labels.reason: Across 12 pairs, descriptions average AUROC 0.76 versus 0.58 for shuffled descriptions; most individual pairs have positive ΔAUROC (r13–r18, r21–r25).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Performance varies by feature and task: some differences over shuffled descriptions are small, feature 132 is not specific relative to its shuffled description, and feature 850 is anti-correlated (r16–r20, r22–r23).
